correctness.rationale: The local time-column de Bruijn graph gives a bijection between each labelled fixed-iterate ring state and a closed walk. Every cyclic SCC at heights 8,9,10 and all needed divisor heights is enumerated from the eight-bit Rule 110 truth table; every edge and minimal column period is checked. At height eight, the only new simple cycle has spatial length eight. At height nine, the additional simple cycles have lengths 6 (three copies), 12 (three copies), 18 (one copy), with temporal period nine. At height ten, every cyclic component has time-column period at most five, specifically one/five/two. These exact facts imply the three formulas for all n. Direct independent bit-parallel state enumeration over all 3<=n<=20 confirms the first cases but is not treated as the infinite proof. Delivered programs report FULL_SPECTRAL_COUNTS_OK and BRUTE_FORCE_OK.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the three shortest previously unclassified temporal-return classes following documented periods through seven in a canonical universal cellular automaton. It distinguishes an isolated 8-period clock, three arithmetic 9-period mechanisms, and a total 10-period obstruction on every ring. The orbit-counts C8<=1 and C9<=8 show a zero-entropy valley contrasting with published exponential temporal-five and temporal-seven population growth. This structural all-size conclusion is sharper than a finite example or an arbitrary invariant and supplies checkable constraints for glider-mode theories.
